answer_1.quote: We evaluate our implementation on datasets with an increasing number of utterances to assess its performance across various tasks. We start with the XSum dataset, consisting of BBC news articles paired with concise, one-sentence summaries... We then scale up to longer outputs using the ROCStories dataset for title-to-story generation, and the DialogSum dataset for summary-to-dialogue generation... Additionally, we test our model on dialogue generation with DeliData.

answer_2.quote: We use ROUGE as the primary evaluation metric to assess the quality and similarity of generated text... Following the evaluation metrics in the literature, we also evaluate the perplexity of generated text... Representation to Text... we tested various autoencoder-decoder configurations using BLEU.

answer_3.quote: Additionally, we employed Gemini-1.5 as an LLM-based evaluator. Using a carefully designed prompt... Gemini-1.5 provided fluency ratings for predictions from the XSum dataset.
methods: LLM-as-a-judge with a prompt for fluency

answer_4.quote: For ROCStories, DialogSum, and DeliData, we recruited 5 participants to evaluate 25 dialogues generated by LD4LG, Flan-T5, and SLD for each dataset... Annotators also rated the gold dialogue output as a reference.
answer_4.guideline: assessing repetition, fluency, coherence, compatibility (ROCStories/DialogSum), and hallucination (DeliData): • Repetition: Check for repetitive tokens or utterances that affect meaning. • Fluency/Grammar: Assess grammatical correctness and fluency. • Coherence: Evaluate logical flow and naturalness of interactions. • Compatibility: Ensure alignment with the story title/dialogue summary. • Hallucination: Detect impossible choices or non-existent participants.
